dek.text: Texas A&M scientists ran an AI structure tool across every pairing of {{number:c2}} curated mitochondrial proteins and kept {{number:c4:1}} likely partners out of {{number:c4}}.

introduction.text: [About {{number:c1}} proteins sit inside human mitochondria, the energy centers of the cell](c1), [and mutations in nearly {{number:c22}}% of them have been linked to human disease](c22).

[The team works in Texas A&M's Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics in College Station](c28). [It turned AlphaFold-Multimer, a tool built to predict the shapes of protein complexes, into a classifier for protein interactions](c7). [It screened {{number:c3}} protein pairs and kept {{number:c3:1}} as likely interactions](c3).

sections.heading: How a pair makes the list

paragraphs.text: [AlphaFold-Multimer is a neural network trained to predict the structures of complexes made of more than one protein chain](c5). [Google DeepMind created it, the release says](c6). [For this screen the authors built a curated list of {{number:c2}} proteins](c2) and asked the tool about every pair among them.

[A pair counts as likely when its mean ipTM score reaches {{number:c8}}](c8). [The authors say that cutoff gives {{number:c8:1}}% recall at a false discovery rate of about {{number:c8:2}}% on their test set](c8). [At that cutoff the screen predicts {{number:c9:1}} interactions involving {{number:c9:3}} proteins](c9). [The paper also states {{number:c11}}% precision for direct interactions](c11).

[More than half of the likely interactions had never been reported before](c13). [Checked against existing interaction databases, {{number:c14}}% were in none of them](c14). [The screen found at least one predicted partner for {{number:c30}} uncharacterized proteins](c30).

[The team ran the same analysis on {{number:c16}} diverse eukaryotes and found interactions among the human hits that held across evolution](c16). [Lab work guided by the predictions pointed to interactions that form the coenzyme Q metabolon](c17) [and mapped the pathway that delivers copper to cytochrome c oxidase](c18).

[About two years of laboratory experiments confirmed several of the predicted partnerships in yeast and human cells](c19). [The team posted the predictions as a free resource called MitoMatch](c20), [which is made up of the predicted interactions](c21) [and is online at mitomatch.web.app](c29).

[The release does not say how many predicted pairs were tested in the lab, only that several were confirmed](c19). [The paper says the method can't give the binding affinity of an interacting pair](c24). [It adds that many predicted interactions may occur only inside a larger complex rather than as true two protein pairs](c25).

[The release cautions that cures for diseases linked to mitochondria may still be far off](c23). [The computing came from Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing](c26), [which the release names among the study's supporters with The Welch Foundation](c27).
